feature: A screen recording keeps the screen's colours and smooth gradients
summary: Recordings are now written by Photonz in 10-bit, in the screen's own colours, at the encoder's top quality: they look like the screen did, dark gradients stay smooth, they start a little sooner and cost the Mac about the same. Settings > Recording > Quality has Smaller files for anyone who minds the size of a recording where the whole screen moves.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default. Numbers and how they were measured: docs/progress/2026-11-15-recording-colour.md (Scripts/recording-colour-drill.sh, Scripts/recording-start-drill.sh, Scripts/recording-latency-drill.sh). Walks: a-recording-opens-at-stop-walk (a real recording, fails unless it is 10-bit HEVC in Display P3), recording-quality-in-settings-walk.

try.do: Look at your own recording of 2026-10-28 beside the same frame with its darks stretched: those contour bands are what every recording had.
Record a dark translucent Ghoztty window over your wallpaper with ⇧⌘5, Return, then Stop after a few seconds.
Open the recording in QuickTime and hold it beside the live window: the purple panes should be the same colour and smooth.
Open the same recording in Photonz and compare the panes with QuickTime's.
Look at the test ramps with their darks stretched eight times, before and after, against a screenshot.
Open Settings (⌘,) and find Recording > Quality, reading Best; try Smaller files on a recording of a scrolling page and compare the file sizes.

evaluate: Does a fresh recording of your dark Ghoztty panes look like the panes on screen, with no bands, in QuickTime and in Photonz?
Is Best the right default, given a recording where the whole screen moves is about four times the old size (a still screen is smaller than before)?
Does recording still start the instant you press Return, and does the Mac feel as light while it records?
Is Smaller files the right word for the other choice, and is Settings the right place for it?
rough: Best costs about 15 MB a second while the whole screen moves (924 MB a minute on the test scene against 237 before); a still screen is 37 MB a minute against 46 before. Smaller files is 118 and 13, with faint one-code-value bands in dark gradients. Chose Best as the default because the banding was the complaint and the load and start are the same; your call if the size is wrong.

Photonz's editor shows video frames as 8-bit pictures, so a dark gradient there steps one code value at a time (measured 1.0 to 1.25 with the encoder's noise, against 0.8 in QuickTime). Any 8-bit picture in the editor does the same; left in the task log.

The processes that record use a little more of the Mac: 13.5 percent of one core against 9.5 (about a quarter of a percent of this Mac), and the whole recording including WindowServer 68 against 63.5 percent of a core. GPU, memory and dropped frames are unchanged.

With the Mac's sound recorded, the stream's first frame still comes about 70 ms after Return, after the drill's square has turned, as it did before (83 ms then): the start of a recording with sound misses the first 70 ms either way.
Exports stay sRGB: a Display P3 colour beyond sRGB is clipped in an exported video, as before; colours inside sRGB come out within two code values.
Current is unchanged: macOS still writes its recordings. No mock covers recording quality; the Settings row follows the Settings window's own system form.
